title: Flicker change blindness
summary: Rensink, O'Regan & Clark's (1997) flicker paradigm: an original and a modified scene alternate (A, A, A', A', 240 ms each with 80-ms gray blanks) until the subject presses SPACE, then reports where the change was (one of four boxes) and what kind it was (appear/disappear, colour, location). The measure is the number of alternations needed to identify the change, compared between changes to central and marginal interests. Scenes are 12 generated photo pairs and procedural pairs; an adaptation, not the original images.
references: Rensink, R. A., O'Regan, J. K., & Clark, J. J. (1997). To see or not to see: The need for attention to perceive changes in scenes. Psychological Science, 8(5), 368-373. https://doi.org/10.1111/j.1467-9280.1997.tb00427.x

deviations.original: 48 colour photographs of real-world scenes (p. 369), not redistributable
deviations.here: 12 photo pairs generated for this project (an image model made each scene and an edit removing one object) plus 36 procedural pairs drawn by src/rensink1997/procedural.py
deviations.reason: the originals cannot be shipped; the procedural generator also gives unlimited new pairs

deviations.original: one change per image, made by the authors (p. 369)
deviations.here: photos: the object's mask comes from the base/edit difference and A, A' are composited so they differ only inside it; colour changes rotate the hue of the object's blue pixels to red; location changes paste the object 114 px (3 dva) along x on a clean plate
deviations.reason: image-model edits never keep the rest of the picture identical, which would add flicker everywhere

deviations.original: five naive observers' brief descriptions; central = mentioned by >= 3, marginal = by none (p. 369)
deviations.here: photos: the same rule applied to five independent requests to a vision-language model (gpt-6.1-sol, 2026-10-14); procedural: a placement rule (ASSUMED)
deviations.reason: no human raters; model describers are not naive observers

deviations.original: CI and MI changes for every type of change (p. 370)
deviations.here: labels came out of the ratings: presence 1 central / 3 marginal, colour 2 / 2, location 2 / 2 (5 central, 7 marginal); the procedural pairs are balanced, 6 per cell
deviations.reason: the photo labels were not adjusted after rating

deviations.original: MI changes larger on average (22 vs 18 sq deg) with similar mean change in intensity and colour (p. 369)
deviations.here: photos: central 20.8, marginal 18.3 dva² on average (pixels whose RGB changed by > 24 levels), intensity and colour not equated; procedural: 18 and 22 dva² by construction
deviations.reason: the generated photographs could not be tuned to the paper's sizes

deviations.original: the observer verbally described the type of change and the part that changed; correct = both right (pp. 368-370)
deviations.here: after SPACE: press the numbered box (1 of 4) the change was in, then P, C or L for its type; correct = both right
deviations.reason: alhazen has keys and a wheel, no voice key or pointer; chance of guessing both is 1/12 (the paper's verbal report was near guess-proof), and a box centred on an object may be easier to guess than chance

deviations.here: whole display frames: 14 and 5 frames at 60 Hz (233 and 83 ms), exact at 75, 100 or 125 Hz

deviations.original: six practice trials, two of each type (p. 369), images not described
deviations.here: six procedural pairs, two of each type
deviations.reason: no test scene may be seen in practice

tasks.title: Flicker change detection
tasks.summary: Cue field 3 s, gray 1 s, then A A A' A' flicker until SPACE (max 60 s), then where (box 1-4) and what kind (P / C / L).

parameters.name: image_width_dva
parameters.label: Image width
parameters.meaning: Width of each scene image.

parameters.name: image_height_dva
parameters.label: Image height
parameters.meaning: Height of each scene image.

parameters.name: background_gray
parameters.label: Gray level
parameters.meaning: Gray of the cue field, gray field and blanks, in signed RGB (-1 black, 1 white). ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: cue_field
parameters.label: Cue field
parameters.meaning: Gray field with a white rectangle that opens each trial (a cue word in it in Experiment 3).

parameters.name: cue_box_width_dva
parameters.label: Cue rectangle width
parameters.meaning: Width of the white rectangle. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: cue_box_height_dva
parameters.label: Cue rectangle height
parameters.meaning: Height of the white rectangle. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: cue
parameters.label: Verbal cue
parameters.meaning: none (Experiment 1), valid (Exp. 3, completely valid) or valid50 (Exp. 3, half valid, half naming another part).

parameters.name: gray_field
parameters.label: Gray field
parameters.meaning: Plain gray field between the cue field and the flicker.

parameters.name: flicker.image
parameters.label: Image duration
parameters.meaning: How long each image is shown in the flicker cycle.

parameters.name: flicker.blank
parameters.label: Blank duration
parameters.meaning: Gray blank after each image (0 removes the blanks).

parameters.name: flicker.pattern
parameters.label: Image order
parameters.meaning: The cycle of images, each followed by a blank: A A A' A' (paper, Exp. 1), or A A' (Exp. 2).

parameters.name: max_flicker
parameters.label: Time limit
parameters.meaning: The flicker runs until the detection key or this long (outcome NO_DETECTION).

parameters.name: detect_key
parameters.label: Detection key
parameters.meaning: Key pressed when the change is seen. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: location_probe.n_choices
parameters.label: Location boxes
parameters.meaning: Numbered boxes on image A after detection, one around the change (replaces the spoken description). ASSUMED.

parameters.name: type_probe.keys
parameters.label: Change-type keys
parameters.meaning: Keys for the type of change (replaces the spoken report). ASSUMED.

parameters.name: scenes.photos
parameters.label: Photo pairs
parameters.meaning: Show the 12 shipped photo pairs.

parameters.name: scenes.procedural_per_cell
parameters.label: Procedural pairs per cell
parameters.meaning: Procedural pairs per change type x interest cell (6 gives 36, so 48 scenes with the photos). ASSUMED.

parameters.name: change_area_dva2
parameters.label: Procedural change area
parameters.meaning: Changed area of each procedural pair; the paper's averages.

parameters.name: location_shift_dva
parameters.label: Location shift
parameters.meaning: Shift of a procedural location change. ASSUMED (Fig. 2's example).

parameters.name: iti
parameters.label: Inter-trial interval
parameters.meaning: Pause between trials. ASSUMED, not in the paper.

parameters.name: paradigm.n_per_condition
parameters.label: Presentations per scene
parameters.meaning: Each scene once per subject, in random order. ASSUMED as once.

outcomes.name: CORRECT
outcomes.meaning: Detected, and both the place and the type of change reported correctly; the only trials in the alternation means.

outcomes.name: MISIDENTIFIED
outcomes.meaning: Detected, but the box or the type was wrong (an identification error).

outcomes.name: NO_DETECTION
outcomes.meaning: No key within the time limit; not served again (the scene is spoiled).

outcomes.name: NO_REPORT
outcomes.meaning: Detected, but a report deadline passed; not served again.

events.name: FLICKER_ON
events.meaning: The first image appears; the reaction time runs from this flip.

events.name: IMAGE_ON
events.meaning: Each image onset in the flicker, with payload image (A or B) and n.

events.name: LOCATION_PROBE
events.meaning: Image A with the numbered boxes appears.
